intended_object: This is a helper ring map R[x] → PolyRing(R[x], n+1). It sends constants c to c, and sends x to x·tail_{i+1}, where tail_{i+1} is the sum of the homogeneous coordinates with index > i. I inferred this from the docstring and from how it is used: it is the coefficient part of `homotopyMap`, the i-th degree-raising map of the simplicial contraction.
explanation:
The body is `Polynomial.eval₂RingHom'`, with the constants embedded through `coefficient ∘ C`. The variable x goes to the element (embedded X)·tail(n+1, i+1). The proof obligation asks that this image commute with every coefficient, and it does: the image is central, because the embedded X and the tail are both central.

The map exists only to feed `substitute` when defining `homotopyMap`, the i-th component of a simplicial homotopy (an extra-degeneracy-type contraction) on the polynomial simplicial ring. On its own it is a building block internal to one particular proof construction, not a standard notion from the literature. So there is nothing to compare it against for generality.

It does what its docstring says: it evaluates the coefficient polynomial at x·tail. This is confirmed by the simp lemmas `homotopyCoefficient_C` and `homotopyCoefficient_X`.
